newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia cuts tax on processed coffees.
newsitem.headline: Colombia cuts tax on processed coffees.

text.p: Colombia has decided eliminate or sharply reduce a tax on its exports of processed coffees in a bid to boost their competitiveness abroad, government sources said Tuesday.
They spoke after Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo alluded to the decision after a weekly policy meeting of the National Coffee Growers' Federation Monday night.

The sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said Ocampo and senior federation officials had decided private exporters should no longer be required to pay steep fees to the National Coffee Fund against their exports of roasted, decaffeinated, freeze dried or instant coffees.
Colombia's annual exports of such coffee total just 500,000 60-kg bags.
The fees on processed coffee had previously been set for July at 597 pesos per kilo of decafe, 308 pesos per kilo for instant and 564 pesos per kilo for roasted coffee.
One government source said the fees would now be cut "practically to zero."
"This decision is a good signal for the market," one private exporter said Tuesday. "It's an important step toward the deregulation of the industry."
